diagnosis.root_cause: Intermittent degradation on this customer's optical fibre path is causing RX power to oscillate between degraded and critical levels, leading to repeated PPPoE re-authentication and session drops.
evidence: The customer has 16 sessions in 24 hours and 94 in seven days, far above the normal 2-3 sessions per day baseline; average session duration is only 71 minutes versus the 11.9-hour network mean.
RX power is currently -27.94 dBm, in the critical range, and the stored reading of -26.28 dBm is degraded.
The seven-day RX series repeatedly swings across a wide range, approximately -24.2 to -28.6 dBm, far exceeding the healthy 24-hour noise floor of +/-0.3 dBm.
TX power remains stable near +2.3 dBm, TX bias current remains healthy around 11 mA, and supply voltage is stable, making laser degradation or ONU power failure unlikely.
Distance remains constant at 302 m, so there is no evidence of a changed fibre path or distance-change event.

All sampled peers on EPON0/2 have materially stronger and stable RX levels, while the OLT and PON port are healthy; this localizes the issue to the single customer's fibre path rather than the PON, splitter, OLT, or router.
The ONU is currently online and authenticated, and the VLAN and RADIUS records are consistent, ruling out an authentication, provisioning, VLAN, or RADIUS fault.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre technicians to inspect the customer's drop fibre, connectors, splices, splitter termination, and ONU patch lead. Clean and reterminate connectors, perform OTDR and optical power tests, and repair or replace the degraded fibre or ONU optics as indicated. Continue monitoring RX power and session frequency after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: RX power oscillates between roughly -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle, crossing the threshold at which the link stops being usable. The session drops follow the signal excursions.
expected_reasoning: Sixteen sessions in 24 hours against a 2-3 baseline, with a 71 minute mean duration
Cached RX is -26.28 dBm, already in the degraded band
Telemetry shows RX oscillating between about -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle
The lower excursions cross -28 dBm, at which point the link becomes unusable
Live RX of -27.94 confirms the signal is currently near the bottom of that swing
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable, so the ONU is healthy
RADIUS is clean with a single consistent entry and no mismatches
Peers on EPON0/2 read normal, so the fault is in this customer's own path
The session pattern tracks the signal excursions, so the optical fault explains the flapping
distractors: The trigger names the session count, pointing at the auth layer
Sixteen disconnects is well within the observed flapping tail and could be read as a CPE fault
